summary:
**SPACE GRAVEYARD — The Machines We Left Behind** is an interactive educational web platform that brings the stories of abandoned spacecraft and mission hardware on the Moon and Mars to life. Developed by TEAM_PRO, the project addresses the challenge of making forgotten space exploration hardware more visible, understandable, and engaging.

Through interactive mission exploration, maps, timelines, hardware information, scientific visualizations, and educational quizzes, users can discover what was left behind, where it is located, and why these machines matter. The platform uses curated information from NASA and Jet Propulsion Laboratory archival resources to connect historical mission records with accessible storytelling.

SPACE GRAVEYARD helps students, educators, and space enthusiasts explore the scientific and engineering legacy of past missions. Our goal is to preserve the stories of these machines, make space history easier to understand, and inspire the next generation of explorers.

**Even when a mission ends, its legacy remains.**
details:
SPACE GRAVEYARD — The Machines We Left Behind

1. What Does Our Project Do?

SPACE GRAVEYARD is an interactive educational web platform that tells the stories of spacecraft and mission hardware left behind on the Moon and Mars. It explores an important but often overlooked part of space exploration: what happens to machines after their missions end?

Users can explore abandoned mission hardware through interactive maps, mission timelines, hardware information, scientific visualizations, and educational quizzes. The platform helps visitors understand where these machines are located, what they were designed to do, why they were left behind, and what scientific or historical value they still hold.

2. How Does It Work?

The platform provides an engaging exploration experience through several features:

  • Moon and Mars Explorer: Switch between the Moon and Mars to discover missions and their remaining hardware.
  • Mission Explorer: Browse and explore historical missions, including Apollo 11, Apollo 15, Surveyor 3, Opportunity, InSight, and Perseverance.
  • Interactive Maps: Explore the locations associated with selected missions and hardware.
  • Mission Timelines: Follow important events from launch and landing to mission completion.
  • Hardware Explorer: Learn about spacecraft components, their original purposes, and what happened to them.
  • The Last Signal: Experience an educational audio simulation inspired by the idea of a mission's final communication. It is a simulation, not an actual NASA transmission.
  • NASA Data Explorer and Visualizations: Explore curated mission information and educational visual representations.
  • Education Mode: Test knowledge through interactive quizzes.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

Space exploration is often remembered through successful landings, discoveries, and active missions. However, the hardware left behind also represents human innovation, engineering challenges, scientific achievements, and the history of exploration.

Our project makes this overlooked history easier to understand and explore. It aims to:

  • Make space science more accessible to students and general audiences.
  • Encourage curiosity about planetary exploration and aerospace engineering.
  • Help users understand the scientific and historical value of abandoned mission hardware.
  • Connect mission history with interactive digital storytelling.
  • Inspire future scientists, engineers, researchers, and space enthusiasts.

Our intended impact is educational: to turn forgotten spacecraft and mission equipment into meaningful learning experiences.

4. Tools and Technologies Used

We developed SPACE GRAVEYARD as a web-based application using:

  • Next.js 14 — React-based web application framework.
  • React 18 — Interactive user interface development.
  • TypeScript 5 — Structured and type-safe application development.
  • Tailwind CSS 3 — Responsive styling and interface design.
  • Framer Motion — Interface animations and transitions.
  • Recharts — Data visualization.
  • Lucide React — Interface icons.
  • Git and GitHub — Version control and source-code collaboration.
  • Vercel — Website deployment and public hosting.

The project is software-based and does not require additional physical hardware.

5. NASA Data and Research

We researched and used curated information from NASA and Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) archival resources, along with relevant planetary science references, to build the mission stories and educational content.

Our selected examples include Apollo lunar hardware, Surveyor 3, the Opportunity rover, the InSight lander, and discarded hardware from the Perseverance landing system.

We aim to present historical and scientific information in an understandable format while distinguishing documented mission information from educational simulations and visual interpretations.

6. What Makes Our Project Creative?

Our creative approach is to treat abandoned spacecraft not simply as discarded equipment, but as historical witnesses to humanity's journey beyond Earth.

Instead of presenting mission information as ordinary text, SPACE GRAVEYARD combines interactive exploration, maps, timelines, hardware storytelling, audio simulation, visualizations, and quizzes in one platform.

The concept connects science, technology, history, and storytelling to create an engaging digital experience for learners.

7. Factors Considered During Development

During development, our team considered:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using NASA and JPL archival references and avoiding unsupported claims.
  • Educational value: Explaining complex mission information in an accessible way.
  • User experience: Organizing content into clear and interactive sections.
  • Accessibility and usability: Considering readable content, navigation, and responsive layouts.
  • Performance: Building a web experience that can be accessed through a standard browser.
  • Transparency: Clearly distinguishing educational simulations from authentic mission records.
  • Future improvement: Identifying opportunities to expand mission coverage, improve visualizations, and incorporate more verified scientific resources.

8. Our Vision

We believe that a mission does not lose its importance when its journey ends. The machines left behind continue to represent human curiosity, courage, and engineering achievement.

Through SPACE GRAVEYARD, we want to preserve their stories, make their legacy accessible, and inspire the next generation to explore beyond Earth.

Even when a mission ends, its legacy remains.
